content.value_statement: Scientific claims can overstate what methods and data support. This skill applies structured checks for validity, bias, statistics, reasoning, and evidence quality.
actual_capabilities: Assesses alignment between research questions, study designs, measurements, and causal claims.
Identifies cognitive, selection, measurement, reporting, and analysis biases.
Reviews sample size, statistical tests, assumptions, p-values, effect sizes, confidence intervals, missing data, and multiple comparisons.
Applies evidence hierarchy, GRADE considerations, and risk-of-bias principles.
Recommends practical improvements to study designs and scientific claims.
limitations: Does not retrieve papers, verify citations, or access external databases without separate tools and supplied sources.
Cannot replace domain experts, statisticians, ethics review boards, or formal systematic review procedures.
Conclusions depend on the methodological details and evidence supplied in the prompt.
Provides structured critique, not clinical, legal, or policy advice.

use_cases.title: Strengthen a Study Protocol
use_cases.description: Find design, sampling, measurement, bias, and analysis weaknesses before data collection begins.

use_cases.title: Review a Manuscript
use_cases.description: Separate fatal validity threats from important limitations and minor reporting concerns.

use_cases.title: Check a Public Science Claim
use_cases.description: Compare claim strength with the underlying study design, evidence, and uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Claim Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scientific claim: [claim]. Identify the evidence needed, likely alternative explanations, and any unsupported causal language.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an initial review of one claim.

prompt_templates.title: Study Methods Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this study summary: [methods and results]. Assess design fit, sample quality, measurement validity, bias, confounding, and statistical interpretation. Separate major and minor concerns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when methods and results are available.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence Quality Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these studies: [study summaries]. Rate evidence quality using relevant GRADE considerations and risk-of-bias domains. Explain disagreements and synthesis limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several studies address the same question.

prompt_templates.title: Protocol Stress Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Critique this research protocol: [protocol]. Map each validity threat to its likely impact. Propose design or analysis changes, then identify unresolved uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced review before preregistration or ethics submission.

output_examples.input: A survey reports that daily coffee consumption causes higher productivity because both measures are positively correlated.
output_examples.output: Overall assessment: the causal conclusion is unsupported. A cross-sectional correlation cannot establish timing or exclude confounding by workload, sleep, occupation, or health. Report the association and request longitudinal or experimental evidence.

output_examples.input: A small randomized trial reports a significant treatment effect but omits confidence intervals and attrition details.
output_examples.output: Important concerns: precision and attrition bias are unclear. Request confidence intervals, participant flow, group-specific dropout, intention-to-treat analysis, and the prespecified primary outcome before rating confidence.

output_examples.input: Three observational studies report similar associations in different populations, but each uses self-reported exposure.
output_examples.output: Convergence across populations supports consistency, but shared measurement bias limits confidence. Compare instrument validity, adjustment sets, effect sizes, and residual confounding before synthesis.

best_practices: Provide the full methods, results, tables, and exact claim whenever possible.
Separate observed data from interpretation, then match confidence to evidence strength.
Ask for conditional conclusions when key design or analysis details are missing.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one checklist item as proof that an entire study is invalid.
Do not infer causation from association without a defensible causal design.
Do not equate statistical significance with practical importance or evidence certainty.

faq.question: Can this skill evaluate randomized trials?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews randomization, allocation concealment, blinding, controls, attrition, outcome reporting, statistical analysis, and applicability.

faq.question: Can it assess observational research?
faq.answer: Yes. It examines sampling, temporality, confounding, measurement, selection bias, adjustment methods, and limits on causal inference.

faq.question: Does it calculate statistics from raw data?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates reported analyses and can suggest appropriate methods, but dedicated statistical tools are needed for reliable computation.

faq.question: Does it perform a formal GRADE assessment?
faq.answer: It applies GRADE considerations, but a formal rating requires complete evidence profiles, domain expertise, and documented judgments from qualified reviewers.

faq.question: Can it verify whether citations are accurate?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Provide the cited sources or use separate retrieval tools before asking it to compare claims with references.

faq.question: How should uncertain findings be handled?
faq.answer: State what information is missing, give conditional interpretations, identify evidence that would resolve uncertainty, and avoid stronger conclusions than the data support.
